posts.title: Data centers are getting their own natural gas power plants
posts.summary: One of the biggest roadblocks to starting up a data center is getting approval to connect to the electric grid—a wait that could last as long as a decade. Some developers aren’t willing to wait and are instead opting to build their own off-grid, or behind-the-meter, gas power plants to fuel the AI boom.   xAI’s…
bullets: As of October 2026, developers have announced plans for over 100 behind-the-meter gas power plants in the US, representing a combined capacity of 115 gigawatts—more than double California's peak power demand.

The primary driver for this trend is speed; developers are willing to pay a premium for on-site power to avoid the decade-long wait times associated with traditional utility grid connection and upgrade processes.

While only a small fraction of these planned facilities are currently operational or under construction, the trend signals a potential long-term shift in how industrial power is sourced and managed, with significant implications for climate goals and grid stability.

posts.title: EU to impose import quotas on hybrid cars from December, China urges adherence to consensus
posts.summary:
The European Commission will impose provisional safeguard measures for up to 200 days, setting quotas at a little over 15% above 2025 import levels.
For details, please visit CnEVPost (cnev.co).
bullets: The European Commission will impose provisional import quotas on hybrid vehicles from all origins starting December 1, lasting for up to 200 days.
Quotas are set at approximately 15% above 2025 import levels, with China receiving the largest allocation at 191,780 vehicles.
The measure is a response to a surge in hybrid imports since 2023, which the EU claims threatens the market share of local automakers.
China's Ministry of Commerce has criticized the move, calling for non-discrimination and reserving the right to pursue WTO dispute settlement.

posts.title: BYD targets acquisition of Ineos French plant as Macron confirms January details
posts.summary:
BYD has entered exclusive negotiations with Ineos Automotive to acquire its vehicle manufacturing plant in Hambach, Moselle, France.
For details, please visit CnEVPost (cnev.co).
bullets: BYD has entered exclusive negotiations to acquire Ineos Automotive's manufacturing facility in Hambach, France, aiming to localize production for the European market.
The potential acquisition would mark BYD's second European production site, following its existing plant in Szeged, Hungary.

French President Emmanuel Macron confirmed the project is part of a broader national strategy to accelerate local automotive manufacturing, with formal details expected at the January 2027 Choose France summit.
The Hambach plant, which previously produced Smart cars and currently assembles the Ineos Grenadier, employs approximately 900 workers.

posts.title: Hope Is Not A Strategy: What First-Silicon Success Really Takes
posts.summary:
Most re-spins are caused by logic and functional flaws, not hard-to-predict physical effects.
The post Hope Is Not A Strategy: What First-Silicon Success Really Takes appeared first on Semiconductor Engineering.
bullets: First-silicon success rates have plummeted to approximately 5% in 2026, down from 14% in 2024, largely due to the rapid rise of custom AI silicon and RISC-V designs outpacing verification capabilities.

The industry is increasingly reliant on re-spins, with half of all projects requiring multiple iterations; at 3nm nodes, a single re-spin can cost tens of millions of dollars and jeopardize entire product cycles.

Formal verification is becoming a mandatory sign-off criterion for leading silicon houses, as traditional simulation-based methods are failing to catch the functional flaws driving the current failure trend.
